title: spec review: R16: orchestrator/stale.py — complete stale-work evidence: interface, tests, dependency, graph and overlapping-merge signals with graded risk and injectable git (AP P12)
spec:
Why: daemon.stale_check (orchestrator/daemon.py:1050-1070) only compares paths moved on the goal branch against the task's scope plus changed files and grades risk none/low/high; the brief (P7) also requires public-interface changes, relevant-test changes, dependency changes, graph-relationship changes and overlapping earlier merges, each recorded with base, goal head, changed relevant paths, risk, action and conflict outcome.
What: new pure module orchestrator/stale.py; daemon delegation is a later integration task, so keep the existing stale_check output keys as a subset.
- evidence(task, *, worktree, goal_ref=None, graph=None, tasks=None, git=None, now=None) -> {"base": task_ref, "goal_head", "moved_count", "stale_paths" (as today), "signals": {"scoped_files_changed": [...], "changed_files_moved": [...], "tests_changed": [...], "interface_changed": [{"symbol", "file", "consumer"}], "graph_relationships": [{"source", "target"}], "dependency_changed": [task ids], "overlapping_merge": [task ids]}, "risk": none|low|medium|high, "risk_reasons": [...], "graph": "used"|"absent"|"stale"|"skipped"}.
- Signals: moved = gitutil.moved_paths(task_ref, goal_ref, cwd=worktree, git=git); changed = gitutil.changed_paths(task, git=git); scoped_files_changed = moved matching scope patterns; changed_files_moved = moved intersect changed; tests_changed = moved paths equal to tests/test_<stem>.py for stems of changed or scoped orchestrator/*.py files; interface_changed = for each moved file, graph nodes defined in that file (node.source_file) whose links (relation calls or imports) reach a node defined in one of the task's changed or scoped files, only when interference.graph_fresh_for reports True for those files, else graph = stale/absent and the signal is skipped; graph_relationships = links between moved files and task files regardless of symbol; dependency_changed = ids in task.depends_on whose merged sha is not an ancestor of task_ref (git merge-base --is-ancestor via the git callable); overlapping_merge = execute tasks from `tasks` merged into goal_ref whose changed_files or scope literals intersect the task's changed or scope paths and whose sha is not an ancestor of task_ref.
- Risk: high when changed_files_moved, interface_changed or dependency_changed non-empty; medium when tests_changed, graph_relationships or overlapping_merge non-empty; low when only scoped_files_changed; none otherwise; unknown when git evidence fails (gitutil.GitError) with risk_reasons ["git_failed"].
- row(task, evidence, action, conflict=None) -> dict for schedlog.append("stale", ...) with task, goal_id, base, goal_head, changed_relevant_paths, risk, risk_reasons, action (recorded|rebased|rebase_conflict|revalidated), conflict paths.
Never mutates git state; never discards work.
acceptance: tests/test_stale.py::test_interface_change_in_moved_file_consumed_by_task_is_high_risk — a graph linking a symbol in a moved file to the task's changed file yields interface_changed non-empty and risk high
tests/test_stale.py::test_relevant_test_change_is_medium_risk — tests/test_foo.py moved while the task changed orchestrator/foo.py yields tests_changed and risk medium
tests/test_stale.py::test_dependency_merged_after_branch_point_is_high_risk — a depends_on task whose sha is not an ancestor of the task ref yields dependency_changed and risk high
tests/test_stale.py::test_overlapping_earlier_merge_is_recorded — another execute task merged into the goal touching a scoped path appears in overlapping_merge with risk at least medium

tests/test_stale.py::test_absent_or_stale_graph_falls_back_and_git_failure_is_unknown — graph None yields graph absent with deterministic signals intact; a git callable raising GitError yields risk unknown and risk_reasons git_failed; row() carries base, goal_head, changed_relevant_paths, risk, action

risks.issue: interface_changed's 'links (relation calls or imports)' filter can't be built on top of interference.load_graph()'s shape, which the spec also requires for the freshness gate (interference.graph_fresh_for) — load_graph() collapses every link to a bare (source,target) id pair and discards the relation field that raw graphify-out/graph.json actually carries.

overlapping_merge needs each merged task's changed_files, but no task record anywhere stores that field (merge() only stamps status/merged_into/sha), and recomputing it via gitutil.changed_paths needs a worktree that's typically pruned after merge.

evidence()'s explicit worktree kwarg is a second source of truth from task['worktree'], which gitutil.changed_paths reads internally with no worktree param — if the two diverge or task['worktree'] is unset, changed-file-dependent signals silently go empty.
risk_reasons content is only pinned by acceptance tests for the unknown/git_failed case; nothing forces high/medium/low signals to populate risk_reasons with anything meaningful.

suggested_spec_changes: Decide explicitly whether interface_changed distinguishes relation types: either drop 'relation calls or imports' and treat any link the same way interference.graph_signal already does, or specify that stale.py reads raw graphify-out/graph.json links directly (with its own freshness check) instead of interference.load_graph()'s reduced shape.

Specify how overlapping_merge obtains changed_files for a historical merged task: either say `tasks` entries must already carry a precomputed changed_files list (and note that this spec does not populate it, so overlapping_merge is scope-literal-only until a later task adds it), or drop the changed_files half of that signal for this task.

Change evidence()'s signature to derive worktree solely from task['worktree'] (matching how daemon.stale_check already does it) rather than taking a separate worktree kwarg, or require evidence() to inject `{**task, 'worktree': worktree}` before calling gitutil.moved_paths/changed_paths so there's one source of truth.

Pin at least one canonical risk_reasons string per non-unknown risk level (e.g. 'interface_changed', 'dependency_changed', 'tests_changed') in the acceptance criteria so risk_reasons can't be satisfied with an empty list.
